hints: At constant speed on a horizontal road, the driving force equals the constant resistance force ($F_D = 650\text{ N}$).
Use the relationship between power, force, and velocity: $P = F_D \times v$, with $P = 20\text{ kW} = 20000\text{ W}$.
walkthrough:
When traveling at constant speed on level ground, acceleration is zero, so the driving force balances the resistance force:
$$F_D = F_{\text{resistance}} = 650\text{ N}$$

The formula relating engine power $P$, driving force $F_D$, and speed $v$ is:
$$P = F_D \times v$$

Substitute $P = 20\text{ kW} = 20000\text{ W}$ and $F_D = 650\text{ N}$ into the equation:
$$20000 = 650v$$

Divide both sides by $650$ to isolate $v$:
$$v = \frac{20000}{650} = \frac{400}{13} \approx 30.769\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx 30.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

hints: When climbing the hill of slope $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{7}$ at constant speed, the driving force must balance the resistance plus the downhill component of weight.
Multiply $F_D$ by the speed $v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find the power in watts.
walkthrough:
At constant speed $v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$ up the slope, acceleration is zero ($a = 0$). By Newton's first law, the upward driving force $F_D$ balances all downward forces:
$$F_D = F_{\text{resistance}} + mg\sin\theta$$

Substitute mass $m = 1400\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, $\sin\theta = \frac{1}{7}$, and resistance $650\text{ N}$:
$$F_D = 650 + 1400 \times 10 \times \frac{1}{7} = 650 + 2000 = 2650\text{ N}$$

Now use the power equation $P = F_D \times v$:
$$P = 2650 \times 10 = 26500\text{ W}$$

hints: Calculate the reduced engine power: $P_{\text{new}} = 0.8 \times 26500\text{ W} = 21200\text{ W}$.
Calculate the forward driving force down the hill at speed $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$: $F_D = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v} = \frac{21200}{20} = 1060\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law down the hill: $F_D + mg\sin\theta - F_{\text{res}} = ma$, and solve for acceleration $a$.
walkthrough:
First, calculate the new power output of the engine, which is $80\%$ of the power found in part (ii):
$$P = 0.80 \times 26500 = 21200\text{ W}$$

At the instant when the car's speed is $v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$, the forward driving force $F_D$ directed down the hill is:
$$F_D = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{21200}{20} = 1060\text{ N}$$

Now sum all forces acting parallel to the road in the downhill direction:
$$\sum F_{\text{down}} = F_D + mg\sin\theta - F_{\text{resistance}}$$

Substitute the values $F_D = 1060\text{ N}$, $mg\sin\theta = 1400(10)\left(\frac{1}{7}\right) = 2000\text{ N}$, and $F_{\text{resistance}} = 650\text{ N}$:
$$\sum F_{\text{down}} = 1060 + 2000 - 650 = 2410\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law $F_{\text{net}} = ma$ with mass $m = 1400\text{ kg}$:
$$2410 = 1400a$$

Divide both sides by $1400$ to find the acceleration:
$$a = \frac{2410}{1400} = \frac{241}{140} \approx 1.7214\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 1.72\text{ m s}^{-2}\text{ down the hill}$$
